bullets: Game 1 of a single-deck session built from an external ranking, not from synergy: 'I asked Royal API what the eight highest ranked cards right now are in Clash Royale, and I have gotten a deck of these eight cards' (t=9-20), with the stated caveat 'just because they're all really good doesn't mean they actually work in a proper deck together' (t=31-36).

Ryley classifies the result himself at t=88-91: 'this looks like a very real bridge spam deck. So it does kind of go to show that bridge spam is really strong in the game right now.' He pilots it that way — Battle Ram, Elite Barbarians, Goblinstein and Cannon Cart at or past the bridge, with Heal Spirit and Barbarian Barrel as the cheap add-ons; there is no back-line tank push in the whole game.

The deck has no building, so the opponent's Hog Rider connects twice (right tower 4858 -> 2345 by OT 1:28); his substitute is a Cannon Cart placed in front of the King Tower when he expects the Hog (t=171).

Against Bomb Tower + Evo Knight + Evo Firecracker he calls the matchup close to unwinnable (t=106-118) and reduces the plan to one card: 'literally the only possible way to win this is just based off of a really good set of Evo E-Barbs' (t=192-196).

The winning pattern is Mother Witch curse plus bridge Evo Elite Barbarians in overtime: Cursed Hogs off the opponent's Skeletons at t=222 while the E-Barbs are on the tower takes the enemy right tower 4603 -> 1700 (t=222-230), and a Cannon Cart / Heal Spirit / Zap finish drops it to 174 HP by t=260 — 'What a win, bro. We were even able to beat the hard counter' (t=261-264).

Elixir shape in this game: 8 Cannon Cart deployments, 6 Goblinstein, 6 Heal Spirit, 5 Mother Witch, 5 Barbarian Barrel, 5 Battle Ram, 4 Zap, 3 Elite Barbarians — the 5-cost pair (Cannon Cart, Goblinstein) carries both defence and offence, and the two 1-2 cost cards exist to keep those pushes alive.

new_deck.rationale: Every win-condition card (Battle Ram, Evo Elite Barbarians, Goblinstein, Cannon Cart) is dropped at or past the bridge to force an immediate answer, with no tank-behind-the-tower push at any point; Ryley calls it 'a very real bridge spam deck' himself (t=88).
new_deck.why_it_works_md: The eight cards were chosen by Royal API usage/win-rate ranking rather than by synergy, but they land on a coherent bridge-spam shell: three threats that demand an answer the moment they touch the bridge (Battle Ram, Evo Elite Barbarians, Goblinstein), a Cannon Cart that doubles as the deck's only real defensive anchor, and four cheap cards (Barbarian Barrel, Zap, Heal Spirit, Mother Witch) that keep a committed push alive instead of building a new one. Mother Witch is the piece that makes the shell more than a pile of good cards: her curse turns the cheap swarm defenders that bridge spam normally gets stonewalled by into Cursed Hogs, which is exactly how this game is won. The weakness is equally clear — with no building and no big spell, a Hog Rider connects freely and a Bomb Tower plus Evo Knight plus Evo Firecracker defence blanks every ground push, which is why Ryley spends most of regulation behind on damage.
